title: Liverpool Player Ratings vs. Chelsea: Reds Triumph in Chaotic Penalty Shootout
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray6:32 PM EDTLiverpool triumphed in the shootout. / Michael Regan/Getty ImagesLiverpool reached the Carabao Cup quarterfinal on Wednesday after beating Chelsea 6–5 on penalties following a 1–1 draw in normal time.

It was a tale of two spot kicks which provided the only excitement of a tepid first half under the Anfield floodlights. Morgan Rogers opened the scoring from the spot following Ryan Gravenberch’s clumsy challenge, but the Reds responded just three minutes later as Cody Gakpo fired home to level proceedings.

The second half yielded more entertainment, with Liverpool forcing some smart saves from Mike Penders, courtesy of efforts from Ronald Araújo and Bradley Barcola. There were also stops for Giorgi Mamardashvili to make at the other end, but neither team was able to find a crucial winner in regulation time.

A hard-fought stalemate forced a penalty shootout, which Liverpool eventually won. Kostas Tsimikas and Ryan Gravenberch both skewed their efforts from 12 yards, but there were misses from Valentín Barco, Emmanuel Emegha and, finally with the 16th kick, Wesley Fofana, which secured a place in the final eight for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Another stellar performance from Trey Nyoni. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesWith each passing match, Trey Nyoni appears increasingly destined for the top.

The 19-year-old has earned rave reviews for some seriously impressive showings in the double pivot, and he delivered another excellent display against Chelsea’s glitzy midfield. Nyoni’s punchy forward passes and defensive awareness shone through, but it’s his enviable composure that makes him such an eye-catching talent.
Of course, there are imperfections in his game which will need to be ironed out over time, but the sky really is the limit for the youngster.

Gravenberch’s silly challenge was punished.  / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesIraola’s rotated team was not without senior experience, and it was one of the club’s older heads who exhibited the rash immaturity of a teenager to gift Chelsea their lead. Moisés Caicedo was going nowhere inside Liverpool’s penalty area when Gravenberch needlessly clattered through the back of him, deservedly handing the visitors a spot kick.

Just over three weeks on from the Dutchman’s red card during the 3–0 defeat to Manchester City, another brainless decision proved costly for Liverpool. With Nyoni sparkling and Alexis Mac Allister back at his best, such errors threaten to cost Gravenberch his starting position in midfield.
Oh, and he missed his penalty in the shootout, too. An awful evening for the midfielder.
Rio Ngumoha thrived against his old side.  / Carl Recine/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*

GK: Giorgi Mamardashvili—7.8: Helpless to deny Rogers from the penalty spot and made some important saves to keep Liverpool level. Then produced a vital shootout stop to prevent Emegha from winning it for Chelsea.
RB: Joe Gomez—7.0: There was the odd issue for Gomez up against Rogers, but he was generally effective against his English compatriot.
CB: Ronald Araújo—7.8: After a heroic performance at the weekend, this was another all-action display from the Uruguayan. Defends at a ferocious speed.
CB: Virgil van Dijk—6.9: Led by example in a much-changed defensive line, racking up some important interventions to snuff out Chelsea attacks.

LB: Kostas Tsimikas—6.9: The 30-year-old was erratic in possession, as Liverpool have come to expect, but there were no defensive lapses against the speedy Pedro Neto. Produced a shocking penalty in the shootout, though.
CM: Ryan Gravenberch—5.6: No excuses for his idiotic challenge on Caicedo, with little else memorable about his performance. Sloppy in possession, too.
CM: Trey Nyoni—7.1: It’s easy to see why Iraola already trusts Nyoni, who plays with the confidence of someone five years his senior.
RW: Lewis Koumas—6.4: Managed just 12 touches during his hour on the field. Zero impact on proceedings.
